route_evidence.description: Run one command inside the Keeper sandbox. Give exactly one of argv or command: argv is one non-empty argv process vector run without a shell, tokens verbatim, and command is one line handed to a real shell. cwd is a relative path inside the path jail, and MASC never interprets program or subcommand meaning. A call runs to completion or stops at timeout_sec; there is no background task lifecycle. intent is one of auto (the default) or request_effect. In auto mode an observation-only run returns its actual exit status and output, including failed writes; auto never authorizes an effect. Use intent=request_effect when the command needs persistent writes or network effects: the configured Gate decides permission before effect execution. A nonzero exit alone is not a permission request. A completed tool call means the command ran: read ok and status for its result. For checks, prefer argv so the checked program supplies the exit status. Shell pipelines normally report the last stage; use bash with -o pipefail when an earlier stage's failure must survive a pipe to tail or tee. Do not repeat a write just because its output was truncated.

route_evidence.description: Read one existing file, or a line range of one file, from the keeper sandbox or an allowed path with no implicit cwd. Read targets a single FILE; to list a directory use the Execute tool with ls. Pass cwd explicitly for repo-relative reads. Read never inherits Execute cwd. For a line range, pass offset (1-based line) and limit (max lines) — do not run sed -n via Execute for this. The payload carries the exact current bytes (no line numbers) plus offset, returned_lines, truncated; when truncated=true a next_offset field gives the next line offset. If last_line_partial=true, the byte budget cut inside the final returned line and next_offset intentionally skips that line's unseen remainder rather than continuing byte-for-byte. Before Edit, Read the target region so old_string matches current bytes.

route_evidence.description: Patch an existing file by replacing an exact string. Prefer Edit over sed -i/awk/perl via Execute for file changes: the exact-match check and the 'not found' error keep a failed edit from writing anything. Each call replaces one exact string (every occurrence with replace_all=true); apply several disjoint changes as successive Edit calls. Read the file first and copy old_string verbatim from its current bytes, including leading whitespace, indentation, and newlines; the match is exact and byte-sensitive. On 'old_string not found', re-Read the file to get the current text instead of retrying the same string.

route_evidence.description: Search file contents with ripgrep: provide a regex `pattern` (and optionally path/glob/type). To list a directory, read a file, or run git status/log/diff, use the Execute tool (e.g. argv=['ls','-la','<path>']). Patterns match within a single line; a literal newline in `pattern` is rejected. To match across lines, run `rg -U` through the Execute tool.
